evidence: Draft judged: 'Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent - can people have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self?' It sits once in CONTEXT.txt, as the paragraph between the FTC/OECD paragraph and the Silva Mind Control quote in 'Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists'. Against SOURCE.txt (the words replaced) the only differences are the full stop plus 'Can' becoming ' - can' and an added 'the' before 'conscious agreement'; the four-item list and the question are otherwise word for word. That is what the_change says (list joined to the question with a dash). The added 'the' is not named in the_change, but it changes no meaning. Meaning kept: the four kinds (conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent) and the question of influence without the adult self's agreement are all there, and no claim, name, number or fact is added (the FTC and OECD statements are in the untouched paragraph before it). The 'is one thing / is another' distinctness of his published guide is not in the words being replaced either, so this change takes nothing further away. Reading it in context: the spaced hyphen used as a dash matches the article's own habit two paragraphs up ('“dark patterns” - designs used to trick and manipulate consumers'), and a list followed by a dash and a question reads as a quick note in his casual voice. There is no em dash, no stock phrase, no hedge and no tidy summary. The question follows from 'influence people without engaging their conscious mind' just before it and leads straight into the Silva quote, so I feel no seam. Tell rows: the only ones I find happening are mild T12 (a four-item taxonomy) and T21 (one packed sentence, a list plus a question). Both are justified here: the four are the author's own published four, the section's first paragraph already uses the same long comma-list voice, and the change adds no item and no job, it only joins. 'conscious agreement' recurs inside the sentence (T26), but the list's first item is exactly what the question negates, so the repetition does a job and was already in the source; not a tell. Everything else is ABSENT: no first person (T01, C03), no run of commands (T02), the setup is visible in the sentence before (T03), no scene or props (T04, T05, T08, T23), 'unconscious receptivity' and 'emotional compliance' are his named terms rather than vague therapy language (T06), no filler (T07), no permission formula (T10), no bridge (T11, T19), no reordering or detector-driven rewording since the wording is the source's (T14, T15), no 'not X, it's Y' (T16, T18), no finished principle (T17), no closer, uplift or restatement because it ends on an open question followed by a quote (T20, T28, T29), no coach register (T22), the question is not answered straight away (T24), no colon reveal (T25), no tic words (T27), no inner-child naming problem (C01), 'their' means the people of the question and 'adult self' is the source's term (C02), no unsupported named-entity claim in the changed words (C04). Linter: 'B4/E15 list or packed sentence' accepted, because the list is the content (four named kinds from his guide) and the context supports it. 'D9 follows the source order' accepted, because a one-sentence paragraph changed only by punctuation cannot reorder anything, and T13 and T09 do not apply at one sentence (the section's paragraphs differ in weight and kind: a long list, a short factual paragraph, this question, a quote, a closing paragraph). No problem found.
